Palanga Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klaipėdos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Palanga's Jewish community may date to as early as the second half of the 15th century — the local Chevra Kadisha's own records, dated 1487, provide the earliest evidence — with an original cemetery once located at the edge of the Tiskeviciai family's park; when that park was later laid out, archaeologists found the burial layers beneath it to be over 200 years old, though no trace or marker of that first cemetery survives today. From 1831, a new cemetery near Naglis Hill on the town's outskirts took over burial registration. Palanga, famed for its amber trade, became known as the capital of Lithuania's summer resorts, and Jews held city administration positions during the interwar period; a 1938 fire destroyed nearly the entire Jewish residential quarter, just a few years before more than 300 of Palanga's Jews were murdered between June and October 1941. The Yiddish linguist and educator Yudel Mark (1897–1975) was a native of the town.
